entities.name: Marcus Valerius Probus
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Marcus Valerius Probus, sometimes called Berytius or Probus the Berytian, was a Roman grammarian and critic who flourished during Nero's reign (54-68 CE).

Born in 40 CE in Berytus, Roman province of Africa (modern-day Béjaïa, Algeria), Probus studied rhetoric and became a prominent figure in the Roman literary circles of the 1st century CE.

Probus was known for his critiques of poetry and his defense of the classical style, which influenced the development of Latin literature.

Despite his significance in Roman literary history, little is known about Probus's personal life, and his legacy was largely overshadowed by that of his contemporary, the Roman emperor Nero.

Probus died in 105 CE, leaving behind a body of work that would be studied by scholars for centuries to come.

One of the most striking aspects of Probus's legacy is the enduring impact of his critiques on the development of Latin poetry, which continues to be studied by scholars today.
